mission.name: The Broken RAG Pipeline
mission.seoTitle: The Broken RAG Pipeline — Production RAG Incident | AhaFrame
mission.description: Debug a production RAG incident where a support agent cites an outdated refund policy even though the current policy exists in the knowledge base.
mission.hero: The new refund policy is in the knowledge base. Your support agent still answered with the old one. Diagnose the evidence pipeline before this reaches more customers.
mission.quick: RAG reliability is a pipeline property: retrieval score, freshness, authority, reranking and context policy must agree on what evidence deserves to reach the model.

brief.title: Yesterday's truth shipped today.
brief.role: You are the on-call AI engineer.
brief.body: A customer asked whether a purchase from 40 days ago can still be returned. The support agent denied the return and cited an older policy. Operations confirms that a newer policy was published two days ago and is already indexed.
brief.objective: Restore evidence freshness and grounding without blowing the 6k context, latency, or cost budget.
brief.stakes: A wrong answer can deny valid refunds at scale.

ui.releaseHint: Run at least one policy before deciding.
ui.waiting: Inspect the evidence, change a policy, then run the pipeline.

debrief.title: More context was never the real fix.
debrief.rule: Retrieval quality is a pipeline property. More context is not the same as better evidence.
debrief.body: The incident was caused by a stale source outranking current authority. Increasing Top-K can improve apparent recall while preserving the wrong source and consuming more context. A robust policy combines retrieval signals with freshness, authority, reranking and a context-retention policy that preserves critical details.
points: Freshness belongs in retrieval policy, not in a prompt apology after retrieval.
Aggressive compression can turn a correct evidence set into a poorly grounded answer.
Trace the evidence path before tuning the model.

takeaways: Chunking, candidate retrieval, reranking, freshness and context policy interact.
The highest similarity score should not automatically override the current source of truth.
A retrieval trace lets you distinguish missing evidence from stale evidence and context loss.
